title: Multi-Invoker Compatibility Shim with Structured-Output Gate and Recursion Watchdog
creator: Aisha Patel
description:
Background:
We continue to expand multi-tool chaining in production flows (function/tool calling + streaming responses + structured outputs). Several customer integrations and internal e2e tests surfaced two classes of failure: (1) incompatible tool stubs that mutate streaming frames and break structured-output parsers, and (2) unbounded recursive invocation patterns when tool results are re-injected as new prompts, causing runaway loops and increased cost/latency.

Goal:
Implement a lightweight compatibility shim (invoker compatibility layer) and a runtime 'watchdog' that together: (a) normalize tool outputs into a well-known framed transport for streaming, (b) validate and gate structured-output shapes before re-injection, and (c) detect and mitigate recursion/loop patterns with soft and hard limits. The solution should be incremental, backward compatible (graceful opt-in), and observable.

Non-goals:
- Rewriting existing tool runtimes.
- Full formal verification of tool schemas (we rely on schema hints and runtime checks).

Design summary:
1) Compatibility shim (invoker adapter):
   - Sits between the orchestrator and tool adapters.
   - Wraps tool stdout/stream frames into a standard envelope: {frame_type, sequence_id, payload, schema_hint}. For non-streaming tools the shim emits a single 'final' frame.
   - For legacy adapters we provide a lightweight shim stub that maps legacy payloads into the envelope, dropping ambiguous control characters and returning a "compatibility_score" header to diagnostics.

2) Structured-output gate:
   - The shim attempts to parse the schema_hint or falls back to JSON/YAML/line-delimited heuristics.
   - If a tool's payload fails validation against the expected schema (provided by the caller or inferred from the prompt), the gate emits an error frame and a suggested rewrite token to the orchestrator (no automatic re-injection).
   - Operators can configure strict | permissive | learn modes. Learn mode records examples for later onboarding.

3) Recursion Watchdog:
   - Each invocation carries a compact provenance header: invoker_id, depth, last_tool_chain_hash. These are small encoded strings attached to requests.
   - Soft guard: when depth exceeds configurable threshold (default 4), inject a non-fatal warning into the response and switch subsequent tool calls to sampled dry-run mode (no external side effects).
   - Hard guard: when depth exceeds absolute limit (default 10) or when identical last_tool_chain_hash repeats >3 times within a single session, abort with structured error and telemetry.
   - Backoff strategy for adaptive workloads: reduce streaming chunk size and convert to synchronous single-call fallbacks under heavy reentrancy.

Compatibility and rollout plan:
- Phase 0 (canary): enable shim in a read-only mode for 10% of internal traffic; collect compatibility_score, gate-fail rates, and false-positive rates.
- Phase 1 (opt-in): expose shim to Dedicated customers via config flag; enable learn mode for legacy adapters.
- Phase 2 (default opt-out): ship as default for hosted API with permissive mode; provide operator controls in console for strictness and thresholds.

Observability & metrics:
- metrics: shim.compatibility_score_histogram, gate.validation_failures, recursion.depth_histogram, recursion.aborts, tool.rewrite_suggestions_emitted.
- traces: span for shim normalization and structured-parse step.
- Logs: include last_tool_chain_hash and session_id (PII-free) along with sampling.

Testing & acceptance criteria:
- Unit tests for envelope framing, legacy mapping logic, schema heuristics.
- Integration tests that simulate streaming + tool result injection with malformed frames.
- Load test demonstrating <5% p50/99 latency impact when shim enabled in permissive mode at 2000 RPS.
- Fallback correctness: orchestrator must handle gate error frames without deadlock.

Rollout checklist:
- [ ] Shim implementation + unit tests merged (PR: link below).
- [ ] Canary config and dashboards created (grafana dashboard id: INV-compat-6).
- [ ] Auto-retry/backoff logic added to orchestrator and SDKs (v0.12.3).
- [ ] Runbook draft for recursion abort incidents published.

Links and artifacts:
- Design doc: https://redwood-internal.atlassian.net/wiki/spaces/INF/pages/678219/Invoker+Compatibility+Shim
- Implementation PR (initial): https://github.com/redwood-inference/runtime/pull/14822
- Canary dashboard: https://grafana.redwood.internal/d/INV-compat-6

Open questions / trade-offs:
- How much schema inference do we do server-side versus encouraging SDKs to provide explicit schema hints? Recommendation: require schema_hint for high-cost I/O tools and default to heuristics otherwise.
- Do we persist last_tool_chain_hash across sessions for cross-request loop detection? Privacy concerns suggest we avoid long-term persistence; stick to per-session memory.

Acceptance criteria (condensed):
- shim.normalization_end_to_end tests pass in CI.
- no more than 0.5% gate false-positive rate during 1-week canary.
- recursion hard-abort correctly prevents runaway in synthetic stress tests.
acceptance_criteria: Envelope framing works for streaming and non-streaming tools
Gate rejects malformed structured outputs with a clear error frame
Recursion watchdog triggers soft warnings at depth 4 and hard abort at depth 10
Rollout can be toggled per-customer and per-environment
